WILLIAM

How does that look in practice? Think of airport security.

You walk down a corridor that only goes one way. You show your passport. You go through the scanner. And the gate staff decide whether you board. No single check catches everything; each one assumes the last one failed.

Northstar has the same four. The corridor: Linkerd and network policy, so the gateway is the only road to the payment tool. The passport: SPIFFE and SPIRE, who is acting. The scanner: agentgateway, which stops anything above fifty thousand euros, whoever asks. And the gate staff: the policy service, reading an OpenFeature flag: up to six thousand euros today, then a person.

And the rule book is locked: the agent can't edit any of it. That's Kyverno.

Two of these get a closer look: the passport, and the gate staff's flag.

Source: Ch 7 (defence in depth); deploy/platform/ (reach, spire, agentgateway, openfeature, kyverno)
